prompts.prompt2:
<pasted_content id="144b">
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

Use Unsplash for images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.
</pasted_content id="144b">

finalReport:
I built the blog: a front page that lists the posts, and two posts about why MCP is great. All schema, media and content went in through the Umbraco MCP server, and all three pages load with every image rendering.

**How to view it**
- The site is running now at https://localhost:44317/ (I started it with `dotnet run` and left it running).
- Posts: `/mcp-is-the-usb-c-port-for-ai/` and `/i-built-this-blog-by-talking-to-umbraco/`.
- Backoffice: https://localhost:44317/umbraco, logged in as admin@example.com / 1234567890.

**What I built, in the order you set**
1. **Content model (MCP):**
   - Five block types in the Blocks folder: Hero, Rich Text, Image, Quote, and Blog Post List (lists the posts, newest first).
   - Two block grids: one for the front page (Hero, Blog Post List, Rich Text) and one for posts (Hero, Rich Text, Image, Quote). The project filed both under `/Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid` automatically.
   - Two page types in the Pages folder: Blog Front Page and Blog Post. A post's body is its block grid; a separate Listing tab holds the excerpt, listing image and publish date for the post list.
   - Two templates, and WWW now allows the blog as a child.
2. **Content (MCP):**
   - Five Unsplash images imported into a "Blog" media folder.
   - "The Model Context Blog" page under WWW, with domain `/`.
   - Two published posts, each made of 6 blocks. I read every document back after writing it to confirm it saved.
3. **Razor, after stopping, building and restarting:** it follows the block pipeline in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
   - Pages call `GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`.
   - Each block has an adapter in [Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/) that maps it to a plain model and calls a ViewComponent, whose view holds all the markup (Tailwind).
   - The post list is built by [BlogPostService.cs](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Services/BlogPostService.cs), registered in [BlogComposer.cs](Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/Composers/BlogComposer.cs).
   - I added block grid column layout and rich text styles to [site.css](Umbraco.Bench.Frontend/src/site.css). The frontend had never been built, so I ran `npm install` and `npm run build`.

uSync exported all the new document types, data types, templates, media, content and domains.

**Review:** I checked all of this against AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md with an independent review, where a second reviewer tried to disprove each finding. It found one real bug: the post list's empty-state fallback could never run, because the value it tested for null throws an error instead. I fixed it, rebuilt, restarted and checked again. There are no errors in the log, no blocks falling back to "could not render", and every image returns 200.

**Things to know**
- The first view build failed because the templates pointed at `_Layout.cshtml` instead of `_Layout`. I fixed that too.
- All five images were saved with their focal point at the far-left edge. None of the current crops are affected, but a narrower or portrait crop added later would be.
- The folder isn't a git repository, so nothing is committed.
